title: SyPS: Measuring Sycophancy Prompt Sensitivity in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.23837v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are known to exhibit social sycophancy, often validating or agreeing with users in socially sensitive contexts. Existing evaluations typically measure sycophancy under a fixed prompt formulation, leaving unclear whether such behavior is stable when the same underlying situation is presented with different sycophancy-relevant prompt variants. In this work, we study sycophancy prompt sensitivity: the extent to which changes in user confidence, emotional framing, social consensus, or validation-seeking language alter a model's sycophantic behavior. We refer to our evaluation framework as SyPS, short for Sycophancy Prompt Sensitivity. Building on existing social sycophancy evaluation settings, SyPS constructs controlled prompt variants that preserve the same underlying user situation while varying sycophancy-relevant social cues. translated_title: SyPS：衡量大型语言模型中谄媚提示敏感性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.23837v1 公告类型：新  摘要：大型语言模型（LLM）已知会表现出社交谄媚行为，通常在社会敏感情境下验证或同意用户。现有评估通常在固定提示形式下测量谄媚，尚不清楚当相同潜在情境以不同谄媚相关提示变体呈现时，这种行为是否稳定。在这项工作中，我们研究了谄媚提示敏感性：即用户信心、情感框架、社会共识或寻求验证语言的变化在多大程度上改变模型的谄媚行为。我们将评估框架称为SyPS，即谄媚提示敏感性的缩写。基于现有社交谄媚评估设置，SyPS构建了受控提示变体，保持相同的潜在用户情境，同时变化谄媚相关的社会线索。我们引入了谄媚提示敏感性得分（SPSS），这是一个实例级别的度量。
tldr: 本文提出了SyPS框架和SPSS得分，用于系统衡量大型语言模型在面对不同社会线索提示变体时谄媚行为的稳定性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the SyPS framework and SPSS score to systematically measure the stability of sycophantic behavior in large language models across prompt variants with different social cues.
